lenses.summary: A lab that speaks by shipping. The founder's last long interview is July 2024; afterwards the record holds terse posts, weights and papers. Under foreign pressure the responses are minimal and sized to the market: the day the app topped the US store it limited new registrations citing 'large-scale malicious attacks'; asked by Italy's Garante it said it does not operate in Italy and that European law does not apply to it, then pulled the app the same day; Korea got an admission of 'partly neglecting' the law, a local representative and a same-day download suspension; Berlin's demand drew no answer at all. Beijing gets different treatment: the labelling rules were implemented on the day they took effect, with an explicit bar on stripping labels. The asymmetry is the finding — it argues with nobody, complies where the state demands it, and withdraws where a small market demands it.

claims.text: DeepSeek limits new registrations the day its app tops the US App Store, citing 'large-scale malicious attacks'.
Asked by Italy's Garante, DeepSeek says it does not operate in Italy and that European law does not apply to it.
DeepSeek removes its app from Italian app stores the same day the Garante questions its privacy policy.
DeepSeek admits to Korea's PIPC that it partly neglected Korean data-protection law, appoints a local representative and suspends new downloads the same day.
DeepSeek does not answer the Berlin data commissioner's demand to comply with EU transfer rules or withdraw.
Liang Wenfeng gives a July 2024 interview explaining pricing and leaves almost no on-record statements afterwards in this record.

lenses.summary: Prices at cost and proves it. V2 shipped at 1–2 yuan per million tokens, about one percent of GPT-4, and the founder said prices follow cost — no losses, no excess profit. It then published the numbers a lab usually hides: V3's final training run at 2.788 million H800 GPU-hours, about $5.6 million; R1's training at $294,000 in a peer-reviewed paper; and an inference-economics post claiming a theoretical 545 percent daily margin, with a disclaimer that actual revenue is 'substantially lower.' The weights stay free — V3.2 shipped open next to an API-only variant — while API prices were cut more than half on the Sparse Attention release. Funding never enters the record: no outside investors, no revenue figures, no capital events. The money story it tells is entirely a cost story, told to developers rather than investors.

claims.text: DeepSeek prices V2 at 1–2 yuan per million tokens, about 1% of GPT-4 pricing.

DeepSeek cuts API prices by more than 50% with V3.2-Exp and ships V3.2 open alongside an API-only variant.

lenses.summary: Quiet at home, quieter abroad. The founder sits at the Premier's symposium on the Government Work Report and, weeks later, at Xi's private-enterprise symposium — no quote survives either. The state's rules get same-day compliance: labelling measures implemented on the effective date. The state's chip push gets engineering, not statements: after reported Ascend training failed — R2 delayed, NVIDIA kept for training, Ascend kept for inference — the next release carried a UE8M0 FP8 format explicitly targeting domestic chips. Foreign regulators get the minimum: a jurisdiction denial in Italy, a negotiated suspension and relaunch in Korea with a privacy notice letting users refuse transfers to China and US firms, and silence in Berlin. Pressed between two states, it does not pick a side in public; it adjusts the format and the notice.

claims.text: Liang attends the Premier's symposium and Xi's private-enterprise symposium without leaving a quote.
DeepSeek implements CAC's labelling measures on the day they take effect and bars users from stripping labels.
DeepSeek keeps NVIDIA for training and Ascend for inference after the reported failure of Ascend training, and builds its UE8M0 FP8 format for upcoming domestic chips.
DeepSeek relaunches in Korean app stores with a revised notice letting users refuse transfers to China and US firms.
DeepSeek answers Italy with a jurisdiction denial and Korea with negotiated compliance, sizing each response to the market at stake.

lenses.summary: The open-weight craft pattern. Every frontier release since V3 ships as open weights; R1 carried an MIT licence and explicit permission to distil, and the V3 line moved from a custom licence to MIT within a year. Release cadence is its own: V3 in December, R1 in January, an R1 update shipped in place of the delayed R2, V3.1 in August, V3.2 in the autumn. Disclosure runs through technical papers, not press: training GPU-hours, inference margins, and a training-methodology document published alongside the labelling compliance. The chip-alignment move is visible in the stack — an FP8 format aimed at domestic silicon in the release notes. The domain read: watch the licence file and the format notes, not the interviews; policy signals arrive as engineering artifacts.

claims.text: Every frontier release from V3 onward ships as open weights, with R1 under an MIT licence that explicitly allows distillation.

DeepSeek releases on its own cadence and ships R1-0528 in place of the delayed R2.
